en: to be remembered; to be recalled

examples.en: What happened that day will be remembered for a long time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 일이 아직도 또렷하게 기억돼요.
examples.en: Things from my childhood are still vivid in my memory.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좋은 선생으로 기억되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: He wants to be remembered as a good teacher.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 많은 사람에게 기억되는 노래를 남겼어요.
examples.en: That singer left behind a song many people remember.
This event has to be remembered in history.

examples.ko: 제 이름이 사람들에게 좋게 기억되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope my name will be remembered well by people.

explain: '기억하다'는 내가 기억하는 것이고, '기억되다'는 사람들 마음에 남는 것이에요. '기억나다'는 갑자기 떠오르는 것이라 또 달라요. 일상에서는 '기억나요'나 '기억에 남아요'가 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I still remember that movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 마음에 남아 있다는 뜻이고 일상에서 아주 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something stays in your memory, and it's very common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I suddenly remembered what happened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 저절로 떠오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a memory comes to mind by itself.

phrases.en: I want to be remembered as a good friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 남들에게 어떻게 기억되고 싶은지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 싶다', you say how you want others to remember you.

explain_en: '기억하다' is you remembering; '기억되다' is staying in people's minds. '기억나다' is a memory suddenly coming back, which is different again. In daily speech '기억나요' and '기억에 남아요' are heard more.

p.n: 추억되다 adds a nostalgic, fond feeling about the past.

examples.en: The man cast his fishing rod far out.
The tip of the fishing rod bent a lot.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 낚싯대만 들고 있는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hold only a fishing rod all day long.
My fishing rod broke, so I bought a new one.
I bought my child a small fishing rod.
I loaded two fishing rods into the car.

explain: '낚싯대를 던지다', '낚싯대를 드리우다'처럼 말해요. 낚시 도구에는 낚싯줄, 낚싯바늘, 찌도 있어서 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The child held the fishing rod tightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 쥐는 동작을 말할 때 '잡다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 잡다 for holding it in your hands.

phrases.example: 긴 낚싯대로 먼 곳까지 던질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With a long fishing rod, you can cast far.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이를 말하는 '긴'과 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 긴 to describe length.

phrases.en: He dangled his fishing rod over the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚싯대를 물 쪽으로 내려 놓고 기다리는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes holding the rod out over the water and waiting.
phrases.en_equiv: to dangle a fishing rod over the water

explain_en: You say '낚싯대를 던지다' or '낚싯대를 드리우다'. Other fishing gear includes the line (낚싯줄), the hook (낚싯바늘) and the float (찌), which are good to learn together.

examples.ko: 아이의 독립심을 키우려고 혼자 자게 했어요.
examples.en: To build my child's independence, I had him sleep alone.

examples.ko: 독립심이 강해서 부모님께 도움을 잘 청하지 않아요.
examples.en: She's very independent and rarely asks her parents for help.
Independence grows little by little from childhood.

examples.ko: 독립심 때문에 아프다는 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: Out of my sense of independence, I didn't even say I was sick.
I want to raise an independent child.

examples.ko: 독립심과 책임감은 같이 자라는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think independence and responsibility grow together.

explain: 나라의 독립이 아니라 스스로 해내려는 개인의 마음을 말해요. '독립심이 강하다/약하다', '독립심을 키우다/기르다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a strong sense of independence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하려는 마음이 큰 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person with a strong wish to do things on their own.

phrases.en: I'm not very independent, so I always ask my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강하다'의 반대로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 강하다.

phrases.en: Children build independence by doing housework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '키우다'보다 조금 더 격식 있고 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more formal than 키우다 and common in writing.

explain_en: It refers to a person's drive to manage by themselves, not a country's independence. It is often used as '독립심이 강하다/약하다' and '독립심을 키우다/기르다'.

examples.en: Reading develops your ability to think.
The teacher developed the child's language skills.
To develop your muscles, you must exercise every day.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 농업을 발달시킨 덕분에 부자가 됐어요.
examples.en: That country became rich thanks to developing its farming.

examples.ko: 악기 연주는 손을 발달시키는 좋은 방법이에요.
examples.en: Playing an instrument is a good way to develop your hands.
I'm looking for a game that will develop the senses.

explain: '발달하다'는 저절로 자라는 것이고, '발달시키다'는 누군가가 힘이나 기술을 키울 때 써요. 능력, 근육, 산업처럼 키울 수 있는 것을 목적어로 해요. 비슷한 말 '키우다'는 아이, 식물, 실력 모두에 쓰는 더 쉬운 말이에요.

phrases.en: I build up my muscles by exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발달시키다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 발달시키다 and common in daily speech.

phrases.en: With practice, you can develop your memory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력해서 키울 수 있다는 가능성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something can be developed through effort.

phrases.example: 산업을 발달시키기 위해 새 길을 만들었어요.
phrases.en: They built a new road to develop the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to state a purpose.

explain_en: 발달하다 happens by itself, while 발달시키다 is used when someone builds up an ability or skill. Its objects are things you can grow, such as abilities, muscles or industries. The simpler 키우다 works for children, plants and skills alike.

dis.h: cause an ability or area to grow

p.n: 개발하다 is not natural with muscles; it suits new products or plans.

en: to be inserted; to be added

examples.en: Subtitles are inserted into the video.
A new word was inserted in the middle of the sentence.

examples.ko: 책 사이에 그림이 삽입된 부분이 있어요.
examples.en: Some parts of the book have pictures inserted between the text.
An ad will be inserted in the middle of the movie.
The song to be added has not been decided yet.
A table was inserted in the document, so it looks better.

explain: 넣는 사람이 주어면 '삽입하다', 들어가는 것이 주어면 '삽입되다'예요. 컴퓨터 프로그램의 '삽입' 메뉴나 영상의 '삽입곡'처럼 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '들어가다'나 '넣다'도 써요.

phrases.en: I inserted music into the video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넣는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, used when the person doing the inserting is the subject.

phrases.en: The inserted song in this drama is good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마나 영화 중간에 들어가는 노래를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A song placed in the middle of a drama or movie.

phrases.en: A comma goes between the sentences.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '삽입되다' 대신 쉽게 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech, this is a simpler way to say 삽입되다.

explain_en: If the person doing it is the subject, use '삽입하다'; if the thing going in is the subject, use '삽입되다'. You see the noun in the '삽입' (Insert) menu of software and in '삽입곡' (a song inserted into a film or drama). In daily talk, '들어가다' and '넣다' are also used.

examples.en: The child colored in the picture.
When you finish coloring, show it to the teacher.
For coloring, use colored pencils, not a pencil.
It was quiet while they played the coloring game.
Painting the wall took a day.
Coloring takes as much time as drawing.

explain: '색칠을 하다'와 '색칠하다' 둘 다 써요. 그림이나 벽에 색을 입히는 일에 쓰고, 머리카락 색을 바꾸는 일은 '염색'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child colors the picture nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '색칠'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사예요. '색칠을 하다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb form of 색칠, meaning the same as '색칠을 하다' but shorter.

phrases.en: My younger sibling likes coloring books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림에 색을 칠하며 노는 공부나 놀이를 말해요. 그런 책은 '색칠 공부 책'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the activity of coloring in pictures as play or practice; the book is called '색칠 공부 책'.

phrases.en: I like coloring with colored pencils.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)로'로 색칠하는 도구를 말해요. 크레파스나 물감으로 바꿔 쓸 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(으)로' names the tool used. You can swap in 크레파스 (crayons) or 물감 (paint).

explain_en: You can say either '색칠을 하다' or '색칠하다'. It is for putting color on a picture or a wall, while changing hair color is '염색'.

en: to set someone at ease; to ease someone's mind

examples.en: The mother reassured the crying child.
The doctor smiled to reassure the patient.
I want to put my worried friend at ease.
I reassured my family by phone.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 말 한마디가 사람을 안심시킬 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes one warm word can put a person at ease.
I spoke slowly in a reassuring voice.

explain: '안심하다'는 내가 마음을 놓을 때, '안심시키다'는 내가 다른 사람의 마음을 놓게 할 때 써요. '을/를'로 사람을 받아요. '달래다'는 우는 아이나 화난 사람의 기분을 풀어 줄 때 써서 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: My friend put my mind at ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙이면 나를 위해 마음을 놓게 해 줬다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-a/eo juda' gives the feeling that someone did it for me.

phrases.en: I held the child's hand to reassure them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-려고'는 목적을 말해요. 안심하게 하려는 이유를 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ryeogo' states a purpose. Use it to give the reason for trying to calm someone.

phrases.example: 괜찮다고 말해서 엄마가 마음을 놓게 했어요.
phrases.en: I told her I was fine so my mom could relax.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안심시키다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is an easier way to say '안심시키다'.
phrases.en_equiv: to make someone feel at ease

explain_en: '안심하다' is when I feel at ease; '안심시키다' is when I make someone else feel at ease, with the person marked by '을/를'. '달래다' is a little different: it is for soothing a crying child or an angry person.

examples.en: Our school's cheering squad gathered on the field.

examples.ko: 응원단은 경기 내내 큰 소리로 노래했어요.
examples.en: The cheering squad sang loudly throughout the game.
I was in the cheering squad in college.
The players took a photo with the cheering squad.
I saw a poster saying they are recruiting for the cheering squad.

examples.ko: 빨간 옷을 입은 응원단 덕분에 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the cheering squad in red, I felt energized.

explain: 응원단은 모임 전체를 말하고, 응원하는 행동은 '응원하다'라고 해요. 응원단에 속한 한 사람은 '응원단원'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I am a member of the school cheering squad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응원단에 속한 한 사람을 말해요. 응원단은 모임 전체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: One person in the squad; 응원단 is the whole group.

phrases.en: The head of the cheering squad led the song at the front.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응원단을 이끄는 사람이에요. '단장'은 모임의 대표라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who leads the squad; '단장' means the head of a group.

phrases.en: When I go to college, I want to join the cheering squad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 새로 속하게 될 때 '-에 들어가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-에 들어가다' when you join a group.

explain_en: 응원단 names the whole group, while '응원하다' is the action of cheering. One member of the squad is called a '응원단원'.

examples.en: The teacher gets the students to focus.
An interesting story held the audience's attention.

examples.ko: 조용한 음악이 학생들의 주의를 집중시켜 줘요.
examples.en: Quiet music helps focus the students' attention.
I need a way to get a child to focus.
I will focus the effort in one place.
I clapped first to get their attention.

explain: 다른 사람의 주의나 힘을 한곳으로 모으게 할 때 써요. 자기가 집중하는 건 '집중하다'예요. 수업이나 발표에서 '집중시키다'가 자주 쓰여요.

phrases.en: The teacher gets the students' attention.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 발표에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in classes and presentations.

phrases.en: Quiet music helps me focus on studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '집중시키다'를 쉽게 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, spelled-out way of saying 집중시키다.

phrases.en: The presentation couldn't hold the audience's attention.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주의를 모으려 했지만 잘 안 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it tried to draw attention but did not manage to.

explain_en: Used when you make other people's attention or effort gather in one spot. Focusing yourself uses the plain verb. It is common in class and presentation contexts.

dis.h: make people or things gather on one point

p.n: 집중하다 would need a different sentence structure (the students focus themselves).

examples.en: Please line up and go in one at a time.
The children got on the bus one after another.
I checked the documents one by one.
The guests arrived one after another.
The names were called one by one in number order.

examples.ko: 일이 많을 때는 차례차례 하나씩 끝내세요.
examples.en: When you have a lot of work, finish it one thing at a time.

explain: '순서대로'는 정해진 순서를 따른다는 점이 중심이고, '차례차례'는 하나가 끝나면 다음이 이어지는 모습을 그려요. '한꺼번에'와 반대로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: When I call your name, come up in order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 정해진 차례를 따른다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, with a stronger sense of following a set order.

phrases.en: I loaded the bags into the car one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나하나 나누어서 한다는 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes doing things one at a time.

phrases.en: Please come in one person at a time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 한 사람씩 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people move one person at a time.

explain_en: '순서대로' stresses following a set order, while '차례차례' paints one thing following another. It is used as the opposite of '한꺼번에' (all at once).
